{"Author":"GitHixy","Name":"LootView","Punchline":"See every item you and your party pick up, as it drops.","Description":"LootView is a live loot tracker for you and your party, with a permanent history and statistics behind it.

WHAT YOU GET

- Live overlay listing every drop with its icon, rarity, quantity, who received it and how long ago.
- Estimated market value of your haul, priced for your home world through Universalis.
- Need/Greed panel that appears while rolls are open, showing each roll and marking the winner.
- Loot tables for dungeons, trials and raids - the duty you are in, or any duty you search for.
- Searchable history you can filter by item name, rarity, zone, high quality and owner.
- Statistics: rarity breakdown, top zones, daily and hourly activity, play streaks and period-over-period comparisons.
- Duty tracker recording your runs, clear times, items per run and personal bests.
- Export to JSON or CSV whenever you want.

GETTING STARTED

Type /lv to open the tracker and /lv config for settings. You can also open it from the server info bar.
Right-click any row in the list to blacklist an item or copy its name.

PRIVACY

Your history is stored locally in your Dalamud configuration folder and is never uploaded. Market prices are looked up from universalis.app and loot tables from garlandtools.org; both requests send only an item or duty ID. Price lookups can be turned off in the settings.

The plugin icon was produced programmatically with AI assistance. Everything else you see in the plugin is hand-authored.","Changelog":"# Version 1.4.0

A complete visual overhaul, plus market value estimates.

- Every window redesigned around one theme: dark glass panels, brass rules and crystal-blue highlights.
- Removed the Compact and Neon layouts. Classic is now the only view and received all of the design work.
- Settings moved from stacked collapsing headers to a sectioned window with a navigation rail.
- New: estimated market value of everything you loot, priced for your home world via Universalis. The running total is independent of how many items the list keeps and has its own reset button. Can be turned off in the settings.
- Statistics charts are now properly drawn, with hover tooltips, in place of the old text bars.
- Statistics are computed off the draw thread; large histories no longer freeze the game when the window opens.
- Fixed an O(n^2) pass over the whole history that stalled the game for seconds on large collections.
- The loot list highlights new drops, marks rarity on every row and sizes its columns to the content.
- The roll window is now a set of rarity-tinted cards with a countdown ring and a crown on the winner.
- New: release notes appear once after each update, and from Settings - About.
- The overlay now waits until your character has finished logging in before it appears.
- Loot parsing recognises "sprig of".
- Fixed a drawing error being able to leave ImGui's window stack unbalanced.","TestingChangelog":"# Version 1.4.0

{"Author":"Faye, Kage","Name":"Better Occult Crescent & Chest Helper Interface","InternalName":"BOCCHI","Punchline":"BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.","Description":"BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.
- No more of that pesky 'walking' or 'finding chests'. That's for losers.
- A cute little Fate and CE panel that'll tell you what rewards it gives AND help you automatically path to it, wowee.
- An extra illegal 'illegal mode' for those of you that would rather be touching grass or playing a game with worthwhile content.

Command prefix: bocchi (alias: och)
  /bocchi → Opens the main window
  /bocchi config → Opens config (aliases: cfg, c)
  /bocchi config list → Lists config keys
  /bocchi config get <key> → Prints a config value
  /bocchi config set <key> <value> → Sets a config value
  /bocchi buff → Start/stop a buff run
  /bocchi tp [fate|ce|pot] → Teleport toward nearest matching activity
  /bocchi illegal [on|off|toggle] → Control Illegal Mode (no arg opens the window)
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-ce → Flag registering CE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-fate → Flag a FATE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-non-pot-fate → Flag a non-pot FATE

Command prefix: bocchi (alias: och)
  /bocchi → Opens the main window
  /bocchi config → Opens config (aliases: cfg, c)
  /bocchi config list → Lists config keys
  /bocchi config get <key> → Prints a config value
  /bocchi config set <key> <value> → Sets a config value
  /bocchi buff → Start/stop a buff run
  /bocchi tp [fate|ce|pot] → Teleport toward nearest matching activity
  /bocchi illegal [on|off|toggle] → Control Illegal Mode (no arg opens the window)
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-ce → Flag registering CE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-fate → Flag a FATE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-non-pot-fate → Flag a non-pot FATE
  /bocchi reload-translations → Reload translation files (alias: rt)
  /och … → Same as /bocchi (legacy alias; also /occultcrescenthelper)

Picks are announced in chat. Every automation has its own toggle and manual edits always win. Includes the beast-pick advisor for every board and a read-only recorder that writes each Crucible screen to the Dalamud log. Use /lazycrucible to open.","InternalName":"LazyCrucible","AssemblyVersion":"0.0.0.0","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.1.1.0","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"Changelog":"v0.1.1.0 (2026-09-21)

- **Beast Feed**: picks the familiar each feed helps most in the fights ahead and confirms it (kin, satiety, no repeats, knocked-out familiars honoured).
- **Shop**: buys the heals, resistances, gear and feed the upcoming fights call for; never sells and never leaves the shop.
- **Spoils**: takes everything when it all fits; otherwise lists the best items first.
- **Campsite**: selects which familiars rest; Rest stays with the player.
- **Treasure**: marks the best choice and explains why.
- **Fight guide** (`/lazycrucible guide`): all five boards, with horn picks and their reasons, dangerous hits, mechanics and what to bring; opens on the next fight.
- **Hands back**: any input made by hand on one of these screens, or AutoDuty running, hands that screen back to the player. Each screen has its own switch, on by default.
- **Error reporting** covers the new screens: a screen automation that keeps failing drops the input in flight, pauses with one chat notice and retries on its own.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-21)

- **First release**, split out of GluttonyCombo: the Beastmaster familiar selection for Crucible of the Unbroken now lives here, and GluttonyCombo keeps the Beastmaster rotation. Both automations are on by default and each has its own switch.
- **Run roster**: on the Bentbranch Meadows entry menu, sets the ten familiars that cover the board's battles best, once per visit.
- **Battlehorns**: on the formation screen before every fight, puts the three familiars that answer that fight's mechanics on the horns (elemental weakness, interrupts, dispels, cleanses, crowd control the enemies are vulnerable to). Knocked-out familiars are never picked; badly hurt ones lose to a healthy familiar that fits nearly as well. The fight itself is never started.
- **Picks in chat**: one line per fight naming each familiar and why it was chosen (`"Announce picks in chat"`). The window shows the latest selection.
- **Manual edits win**: a roster or horn change made by hand (or by another tool) stops the automation for that screen, and a roster edited that way is kept for the rest of that visit.
- **Stands down for AutoDuty**: while AutoDuty is running a board (it picks its own familiar team), the familiar screens are left alone (`"Stand down while AutoDuty is running"`, on by default).
- **Fixed** (carried over from GluttonyCombo testing builds): the item shop's Beast Feed screen was treated as the Battlehorn screen, so feeding a familiar after the elite fight could fail or move the feed target. The feeding and campsite screens are now never touched.
- **Fixed** (carried over): a run roster cleared and rebuilt on the entry menu (by hand or by AutoDuty) is no longer overwritten mid-edit.
- **Beast-pick advisor**: picks for every battle on every board, the board roster and familiars worth capturing, under "Beast picks by battle".
- **Screen recorder** (`"Record Crucible screens to the log"`, read-only): writes each Crucible screen and every button pressed on it to the Dalamud log, groundwork for automating the path, spoils, treasure, shop, feeding, campsite and beast gear screens.
- Stands down with a chat notice while a GluttonyCombo version that still fills familiars itself is loaded.
- **Problem reports**: `/lazycrucible report <what happened>` or the "Report a problem" button writes a report to the plugin log with the zone, job, recent familiar-selection and screen lines, and the full contents of the Crucible screens that are open.
- **Error reporting**: an error is written as one line carrying the plugin version, build, zone, job and the full stack with file and line numbers. A part that keeps failing (familiar selection, the screen recorder, or its event and click logs) pauses with one chat notice and retries on its own; manual edits are still detected while the event log is paused.
- `/lazycrucible` opens the window; `/lazycrucible changelog` shows this list.","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/tree/main/src/LazyCrucible","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"IsHide":false,"IsTestingExclusive":true,"DownloadLinkInstall":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyCrucible/testing/testing.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyCrucible/testing/testing.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyCrucible/testing/testing.zip","Tags":["beastmaster","bst","crucible","unbroken","familiar","battlehorn","automation"],"CategoryTags":["jobs","utility"],"IconUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/LalaImages/lazycrucible-icon.png","ImageUrls":[""],"DownloadCount":0,"LastUpdate":"0"}

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"AutoPotion","Punchline":"Per-job HP, MP, and deep dungeon potion automation.","Description":"Auto-uses the highest-tier HP potion, MP potion (Ether), and the deep dungeon regen potion (Sustaining / Eurekan / Orthos / Pilgrim's) at configurable thresholds. Each potion's threshold and on/off state is stored per-job, so casters and tanks can have completely different setups.","InternalName":"AutoPotion","AssemblyVersion":"0.2.5.0","Changelog":"v0.2.5.0 (2026-09-05)

- New per-job option: "Auto-use Echo Drops when silenced". When it is on and Silence lands (mob silence spells, AoE silences, deep dungeon traps), AutoPotion uses Echo Drops from inventory to cure it automatically. Item use is not blocked by Silence, so the cure works exactly when nothing else can.
- OFF by default like every option, and per job like the rest: tick the new box in the settings window for the jobs it should apply to. With it off (the default) nothing changes - not even a status check.
- It reuses the same machinery as the potions: HQ Echo Drops are preferred over normal ones, the shared 750 ms cooldown after any potion use applies, and a Silence that arrives during that cooldown is cured on the next tick.
- If the diagnostic tap is enabled, the cure logs as an `e` event; when it cannot fire the near-miss reasons are `edblocked` (on cooldown / blocked) or `ednostock` (none in the bags).
- No change to potion behaviour. HP/MP/regen thresholds, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before.

v0.2.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added an optional "Log potion decisions" diagnostic, OFF by default. Turn it on with `/autopotion telemetry on` or the new Advanced / Diagnostics section of the settings window, and AutoPotion writes one line to its plugin log every time it uses a potion, plus a rate-limited line when a threshold was crossed and nothing fired.
- Purpose: the log line records the HP%, the MP%, the threshold that was in force and the job, so a threshold can be verified after the fact instead of guessed at. Nothing leaves the machine - the lines only go to the local Dalamud plugin log.
- The "nothing fired" lines say WHY in a short code: `hpover` (a potion was available but the heal would have been wasted), `hpblocked` / `mpblocked` / `rgblocked` (on cooldown or blocked by a status), `hpnostock` / `mpnostock` / `rgnostock` (none left in inventory) and `rgrehab` (Rehabilitation still up in a deep dungeon).
- These lines are heavily rate-limited on purpose: a repeated state logs once, not once per frame. Measured against 214 minutes of real play the near-miss lines come out under one line per minute, so the log stays readable.
- No change to potion behaviour. Thresholds, per-job profiles, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before, and with the setting off (the default) the plugin does not even build a log line.

v0.2.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added the in-game "What's new" popup. After AutoPotion updates, its changelog now opens once inside the game so the changes are visible without a trip to GitHub. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyRetainerLive","Punchline":"Real-time retainer venture countdowns for your dashboard.","Description":"Serves the logged-in character's live retainer and venture state on loopback HTTP (127.0.0.1:10504) so the ffxiv dashboard relay can show real-time venture countdowns instead of AutoRetainer's occasionally-stale file cache.","InternalName":"LazyRetainerLive","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.0.1","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.1.0.1","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"Changelog":"v0.1.0.1 (2026-09-05)


- Corrected a wrong claim in the v0.1.0.0 notes below (and on the mod's web page): **the endpoint does not answer 503 on logout.** Once logged in, it keeps serving that character's last known retainer state - including at the title screen - and only ever answers 503 if it has never read the retainer table at all since the plugin loaded (i.e. it started at the title screen and no login has happened yet). That freeze is deliberate and is the better behaviour: measured previously the frozen live snapshot was still *newer* than AutoRetainer's file, so falling back to the file on logout would have shown the dashboard **older** data, not fresher. No behaviour was changed here - only the description was wrong.
- The settings window no longer reports "serving live snapshot" while logged out. It now distinguishes three states: no snapshot yet, serving a live snapshot, or serving the last-known snapshot while the game is in transition.


- For anything scripting against this endpoint: `readAt` is the time the request was **served**, not the time the data was read from the game, so it does not reveal how stale a frozen snapshot is. Use the settings window (or `/lazyretainerlive debug`) to tell live from frozen.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-05)


- First release. LazyRetainerLive reads the logged-in character's LIVE retainer table (the same in-memory data AutoRetainer uses to drive its own countdowns) and serves it as JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:10504/retainers`, so the ffxiv dashboard's retainer panel can show venture countdowns that update the moment a venture is collected instead of whenever AutoRetainer next saves its config file.
- When not logged in (or the live table has no data yet) the endpoint answers HTTP 503, which tells the dashboard relay to fall back to AutoRetainer's file. Loopback only - the port is never reachable from other machines.


- Companion of AutoRetainer - it reads, it never writes, assigns, or collects anything. Settings: Enabled (default on) and loopback port (default 10504). - **Fixed** (carried over): a run roster cleared and rebuilt on the entry menu (by hand or by AutoDuty) is no longer overwritten mid-edit.

- Stands down with a chat notice while a GluttonyCombo version that still fills familiars itself is loaded.
- **Problem reports**: `/lazycrucible report <what happened>` or the "Report a problem" button writes a report to the plugin log with the zone, job, recent familiar-selection and screen lines, and the full contents of the Crucible screens that are open.
- **Error reporting**: an error is written as one line carrying the plugin version, build, zone, job and the full stack with file and line numbers. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyFoodBuff","Punchline":"Never forget to eat your food again.","Description":"Auto-eats food in combat duties with per-job selection, auto-select based on best stats, and a low-food warning.","InternalName":"LazyFoodBuff","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.4.0","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/tree/main/src/LazyFoodBuff","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"IsHide":false,"IsTestingExclusive":false,"DownloadLinkInstall":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyFoodBuff/latest/latest.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyFoodBuff/latest/latest.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyFoodBuff/testing/testing.zip","Tags":["auto","food","buff","duty","lazy"],"CategoryTags":["utility"],"IconUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/LalaImages/lazyfoodbuff-icon.png","ImageUrls":[""],"DownloadCount":0,"LastUpdate":"0","Changelog":"v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-21)

- **"Only eat in combat duties" now covers Crucible of the Unbroken.** The five boards count as combat duties, and so does the Bentbranch Meadows entry area while playing Beastmaster (the one job that can enter), so the meal is eaten before a run starts. Eating before entry matters: a meal eaten inside does not refill HP to the raised maximum.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Optional decision diagnostics, off by default. Turn on "Log food decisions" (settings window, Advanced / Diagnostics) or run `/lazyfoodbuff telemetry on`, and every time the plugin settles on a food for the current job it writes one line to the plugin log: the food it picked, its score, and the runner-ups it beat — plus a second line when that food is actually eaten. The point is the runner-ups: "picked X at 41.20 over Y at 40.80" is the shape of evidence that can eventually say whether the auto-select weights are right. Nothing leaves the machine; the lines only go to the local plugin log.

- Honest caveat: this is a data-collection investment, not an answer. The outcome side (what a food actually did to damage) needs weeks of encounter data before it says anything statistically — the plugin log will quietly accumulate the decision half in the meantime.
- Nothing about food selection changed. When the toggle is off, the only cost is one boolean read.

v0.1.3.1 (2026-09-05)

- The "What's new" popup now opens after this very update. 0.1.3.0 stayed silent the first time it ran because it had no record of the last version shown; the gate now tells an updated plugin (settings file already present) apart from a brand-new install (none yet) and only the latter stays quiet (`ChangelogGate.Options.ExistingInstall`, read from `pi.ConfigFile.Exists`.

- Nothing else changed. The notes can be reopened later with `/lazyfoodbuff changelog`.

v0.1.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- In-game "What's new" popup. After every update, the first time the character is logged in and out of combat, LazyFoodBuff opens a window with the release notes for every version since the last one shown. It appears once per update; pressing "Got it" (or closing it) keeps it quiet until the next update.
- `/lazyfoodbuff changelog` (or `whatsnew`) reopens the release notes at any time.
- "Open changelog on GitHub" button in the popup links to the full CHANGELOG for this plugin.

- This is the pilot of a standing rule for every lalalazy plugin: the popup code is shared across plugins and each plugin embeds its own release notes at build time. New config field `Configuration.LastSeenChangelogVersion`; on the first build carrying the feature it records the running version silently and does not open.
- The popup never opens during combat, inside a duty, while zoning, or in a cutscene - it waits until the character is free.
- `/lazyfoodbuff` with no argument still opens these settings.","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.1.5.0","_SourceId":"dajoey-lalalazy","_SourceName":"dajoey / lalalazy","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/pluginmaster.json","_Category":"automation"}

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyRetainerLive","Punchline":"Real-time retainer venture countdowns for your dashboard.","Description":"Serves the logged-in character's live retainer and venture state on loopback HTTP (127.0.0.1:10504) so the ffxiv dashboard relay can show real-time venture countdowns instead of AutoRetainer's occasionally-stale file cache.","InternalName":"LazyRetainerLive","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.0.1","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.1.0.1","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"Changelog":"v0.1.0.1 (2026-09-05)


- Corrected a wrong claim in the v0.1.0.0 notes below (and on the mod's web page): **the endpoint does not answer 503 on logout.** Once logged in, it keeps serving that character's last known retainer state - including at the title screen - and only ever answers 503 if it has never read the retainer table at all since the plugin loaded (i.e. it started at the title screen and no login has happened yet). That freeze is deliberate and is the better behaviour: measured previously the frozen live snapshot was still *newer* than AutoRetainer's file, so falling back to the file on logout would have shown the dashboard **older** data, not fresher. No behaviour was changed here - only the description was wrong.
- The settings window no longer reports "serving live snapshot" while logged out. It now distinguishes three states: no snapshot yet, serving a live snapshot, or serving the last-known snapshot while the game is in transition.


- For anything scripting against this endpoint: `readAt` is the time the request was **served**, not the time the data was read from the game, so it does not reveal how stale a frozen snapshot is. Use the settings window (or `/lazyretainerlive debug`) to tell live from frozen.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-05)


- First release. LazyRetainerLive reads the logged-in character's LIVE retainer table (the same in-memory data AutoRetainer uses to drive its own countdowns) and serves it as JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:10504/retainers`, so the ffxiv dashboard's retainer panel can show venture countdowns that update the moment a venture is collected instead of whenever AutoRetainer next saves its config file.
- When not logged in (or the live table has no data yet) the endpoint answers HTTP 503, which tells the dashboard relay to fall back to AutoRetainer's file. Loopback only - the port is never reachable from other machines.


- Companion of AutoRetainer - it reads, it never writes, assigns, or collects anything. Settings: Enabled (default on) and loopback port (default 10504). Commands: `/lazyretainerlive` opens settings, `/lazyretainerlive debug` dumps listener + snapshot state, `/lazyretainerlive changelog` reopens this popup.
- Why this exists: AutoRetainer's `DefaultConfig.json` (which feeds the dashboard today) is saved only at AutoRetainer's own save points, so its venture rows can be tens of minutes stale while ventures are actually completing. The countdown for the logged-in character lives in the game's memory - this plugin is a small read-only window onto it.","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/tree/main/src/LazyRetainerLive","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"IsHide":false,"IsTestingExclusive":false,"DownloadLinkInstall":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyRetainerLive/latest/latest.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyRetainerLive/latest/latest.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/plugins/LazyRetainerLive/testing/testing.zip","Tags":["retainers","ventures","dashboard","http","lazy"],"CategoryTags":["utility"],"IconUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/LalaImages/lazyretainerlive-icon.png","ImageUrls":[""],"DownloadCount":0,"LastUpdate":"0","_SourceId":"dajoey-lalalazy","_SourceName":"dajoey / lalalazy","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/pluginmaster.json","_Category":"automation"}

- **Beast Feed**: picks the familiar each feed helps most in the fights ahead and confirms it (kin, satiety, no repeats, knocked-out familiars honoured).
- **Shop**: buys the heals, resistances, gear and feed the upcoming fights call for; never sells and never leaves the shop.
- **Spoils**: takes everything when it all fits; otherwise lists the best items first.
- **Campsite**: selects which familiars rest; Rest stays with the player.
- **Treasure**: marks the best choice and explains why.
- **Fight guide** (`/lazycrucible guide`): all five boards, with horn picks and their reasons, dangerous hits, mechanics and what to bring; opens on the next fight.
- **Hands back**: any input made by hand on one of these screens, or AutoDuty running, hands that screen back to the player. Each screen has its own switch, on by default.
- **Error reporting** covers the new screens: a screen automation that keeps failing drops the input in flight, pauses with one chat notice and retries on its own.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-21)

- **First release**, split out of GluttonyCombo: the Beastmaster familiar selection for Crucible of the Unbroken now lives here, and GluttonyCombo keeps the Beastmaster rotation. Both automations are on by default and each has its own switch.
- **Run roster**: on the Bentbranch Meadows entry menu, sets the ten familiars that cover the board's battles best, once per visit.
- **Battlehorns**: on the formation screen before every fight, puts the three familiars that answer that fight's mechanics on the horns (elemental weakness, interrupts, dispels, cleanses, crowd control the enemies are vulnerable to). Knocked-out familiars are never picked; badly hurt ones lose to a healthy familiar that fits nearly as well. The fight itself is never started.
- **Picks in chat**: one line per fight naming each familiar and why it was chosen (`"Announce picks in chat"`). The window shows the latest selection.
- **Manual edits win**: a roster or horn change made by hand (or by another tool) stops the automation for that screen, and a roster edited that way is kept for the rest of that visit.
- **Stands down for AutoDuty**: while AutoDuty is running a board (it picks its own familiar team), the familiar screens are left alone (`"Stand down while AutoDuty is running"`, on by default).
- **Fixed** (carried over from GluttonyCombo testing builds): the item shop's Beast Feed screen was treated as the Battlehorn screen, so feeding a familiar after the elite fight could fail or move the feed target. The feeding and campsite screens are now never touched.
- **Fixed** (carried over): a run roster cleared and rebuilt on the entry menu (by hand or by AutoDuty) is no longer overwritten mid-edit.
- **Beast-pick advisor**: picks for every battle on every board, the board roster and familiars worth capturing, under "Beast picks by battle".
- **Screen recorder** (`"Record Crucible screens to the log"`, read-only): writes each Crucible screen and every button pressed on it to the Dalamud log, groundwork for automating the path, spoils, treasure, shop, feeding, campsite and beast gear screens.
- Stands down with a chat notice while a GluttonyCombo version that still fills familiars itself is loaded.
- **Problem reports**: `/lazycrucible report <what happened>` or the "Report a problem" button writes a report to the plugin log with the zone, job, recent familiar-selection and screen lines, and the full contents of the Crucible screens that are open.
- **Error reporting**: an error is written as one line carrying the plugin version, build, zone, job and the full stack with file and line numbers. A part that keeps failing (familiar selection, the screen recorder, or its event and click logs) pauses with one chat notice and retries on its own; manual edits are still detected while the event log is paused.
